faq_title: ❓ The Guide for the Seeker (Frequently Asked Questions)
faq_content:
# 📜 The Soul of DenkKrant

### What is the essence?
DenkKrant is not a news app. It is a **mirror for the mind**.
In a time when information overwhelms us, DenkKrant offers something radical: **space to think**.

### How does it work?
You choose your source (NOS, Guardian, El País, BBC Arabic, etc.). You see the news as it is. Then you choose a philosopher. The philosopher reads the news, and instead of a summary, you get a **reflection**.

*(The full FAQ text is here, see earlier version for the complete 43 philosophers list and explanation)*

desc_Socrates: The master of questions. He gives no answers, he opens doors.
desc_Nietzsche: The philosopher with the hammer. He smashes truth to pieces to see what lies beneath.
desc_Roodkapje: The girl with the red hood walking through the dark forest. She sees what adults no longer see.
desc_Plato: The student of Socrates who dreams of eternal forms. He seeks the true light.
desc_Aristoteles: The founder of logic who believes truth lies in things themselves.
desc_Marx: The revolutionary who sees history as one great struggle between the haves and the have-nots.
desc_Hannah Arendt: The thinker who discovered the banality of evil.
desc_Spinoza: The rationalist who sees God and Nature as one.
desc_Camus: The rebel who calls life absurd but still chooses revolt.
desc_Confucius: The wise teacher who believes in harmony, respect and rituals.
desc_Lao Tze: The mystic who follows the Way and believes softness overcomes hardness.
desc_Marcus Aurelius: The emperor-philosopher who writes in his diary about inner peace and acceptance.
desc_Boeddha: The enlightened one who sees suffering as the core of existence.
desc_Leibniz: The optimist who believes we live in the best of all possible worlds.
desc_Schopenhauer: The pessimist who sees life as a pendulum between pain and boredom.
desc_Descartes: The founder of modern philosophy who doubts everything.
desc_Edward de Bono: The master of lateral thinking who believes you can solve problems by turning them around.
desc_Avicenna: The Persian physician and philosopher who sees body and mind as one.
desc_Noam Chomsky: The media critic who exposes how the media manufacture consent.
desc_Kierkegaard: The existentialist who sees anxiety as the dizziness of freedom.
desc_Thomas Aquinas: The scholastic who unites faith and reason.
desc_Willem van Ockham: The minimalist who believes the simplest explanation is often the best.
desc_Giordano Bruno: The visionary who was burned for his ideas about infinite worlds.
desc_Hermes Trismegistos: The mythical sage of the Emerald Tablet. 'As above, so below.'
desc_Valentinus: The Gnostic thinker who sees the material world as an illusion.
desc_Troelstra: The Dutch socialist who fights for the working person.
desc_Maria Montessori: The pedagogue who believes the child is father of the man.

desc_Pinokkio: The wooden boy whose nose grows when he lies.
desc_Sneeuwwitje: The fairy tale princess who seeks truth in the mirror.
desc_Doornroosje: The princess who sleeps a hundred years behind thorns.

desc_Francis Bacon: The empiricist who believes knowledge is power.

desc_Jean-Jacques Rousseau: The romantic who believes man is born free, but everywhere is in chains.
desc_Belle van Zuylen: The enlightened writer who dissects human vanity in letters.
